task: leetlab is a client-side LeetCode-style practice app (React 19 + Vite + Zustand; no backend). Add a feature to generate new problems (not already in the problem bank) using an LLM — local or paid, supporting BOTH Anthropic and OpenAI APIs. Calls are browser-direct; API keys are entered by the user and stored in-app (localStorage). Generated problems must be persistent in localStorage (merged with the built-in PROBLEM_BANK at runtime). A generated problem goes through a review-before-add workflow where the user accepts or discards it, and dedupe against existing problems is enforced. Also add import/export: full-state backup/restore covering progress (solvedAt), saved code, custom test cases, submissions, and the generated/custom problem bank.

analysis.objective: Add a client-side "generate new problem" feature to leetlab that produces problems via Anthropic, OpenAI, or OpenAI-compatible local endpoints using browser-direct calls with user-entered API keys stored in localStorage, routes each result through a review-before-add accept/discard gate with dedupe against the merged problem bank, persists accepted generated problems in localStorage, and adds full-state JSON backup/restore covering progress, saved code, custom test cases, submissions, and the generated problem bank.
analysis.successDefinition: Done when (1) a user can pick a provider (Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible local), enter an API key persisted to localStorage, and generate a valid Problem (both fn and class modes) that appears in a review screen showing title, signature (fnName + mode), and test preview; (2) Accept enforces dedupe against PROBLEM_BANK and already-accepted generated problems — slug/title/signature collisions are rejected with a visible message, never silently added — and the accepted problem is persisted so it appears in the problem list and in getProblem/sidebar alongside built-ins across reloads; (3) Discard leaves the bank unchanged; (4) Export writes a single versioned JSON capturing the persisted Zustand slice (lang, split, lastSlug, problems: solvedAt, js/ts, cases, subs) plus generated problems, and Import validates and restores it so the app behaves identically, while malformed or wrong-version files fail with a clear error and leave the live store untouched; (5) malformed LLM output is re-prompted or rejected, never persisted; (6) `npm run build` (tsc + vite) and `npm run lint` pass.
assumptions: PROBLEM_BANK stays a static module constant in src/infrastructure/problemBank.ts; generated problems live in a new persisted slice (e.g. generatedProblems added to the Zustand store and its partialize) and are merged with PROBLEM_BANK at read time (getProblem and the sidebar list), rather than mutating the PROBLEM_BANK array.
API keys are stored in a separate localStorage key (e.g. leetlab.apiKeys), masked in the UI, and are excluded from full-state export/import to avoid spreading credentials in backup files.

The Zustand persist key `leetlab.v2` defines the persisted state boundary; full-state export covers that partialized slice (lang, split, lastSlug, problems) plus the generated problem bank — matching the user's listed fields (solvedAt, saved code js/ts, custom cases, subs).

Local providers (Ollama/LM Studio) are reachable via a user-configured base URL exposing an OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions; CORS enablement on that endpoint is the provider's/user's responsibility.

LLM output is parsed into the existing Problem shape (slug, num, title, difficulty, tags, fnName, mode, starter.js/ts, tests, hints, desc); a failed parse triggers a re-prompt or rejection, never a silent accept.
Dedupe uniqueness is keyed primarily by slug, with additional title/signature collision checks, evaluated at accept time as specified.
Discarded problems are not persisted (no recycle bin / review history); the review queue is in-memory for the current session only.
risks: API keys in localStorage are readable by any script executing on the page (XSS exfiltration) and by anyone with device access — this is inherent to the user-chosen browser-direct model; mitigate with masked inputs, never logging keys, and excluding keys from exports, but the residual risk cannot be fully removed client-side.

Browser CORS: Anthropic requires the anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access header (which disables certain abuse-detection behaviors), Anthropic/OpenAI may reject browser-origin requests without it, and local endpoints (Ollama/LM Studio) must enable CORS themselves — a misconfigured local server yields opaque network failures that are hard to distinguish from bad-request errors.

LLM output validity: models can emit tests that do not match the declared signature, tests that are not JSON-serializable or use undefined/functions, or near-duplicate problems; without validation + re-prompt logic the runner can break or the bank can accumulate junk.

Dedupe is enforced only at accept time (per spec), so generation can produce a duplicate the user must discard — the flow must surface a clear 'duplicate' state rather than silently adding or silently dropping the result.

Import of malformed, truncated, or wrong-version state could corrupt the live store or the runtime merge; import needs schema validation and a version field, and must not clobber current state on failure.

Zustand persist currently partializes away several live fields (caseMarks, lastRuns, tsStatus, activeResultTab); 'full-state' export must be defined against what is actually persisted, otherwise the work creeps into persisting intentionally ephemeral fields.
outOfScope: No backend/proxy for LLM calls — browser-direct only, per the user's access model; there is no server to hold keys or relay requests.
No authentication, authorization, or multi-user sync — this is a single-browser local app with no user accounts.
No editing or management of generated problems after acceptance (no modifying tests/starter of an already-added generated problem).
No persistence or review history for discarded problems — the review queue is session-only, no recycle bin.
No cost/rate-limit management or streaming/abort UX for generation (no request budgets, token counters, or pricing display).
No new problem kinds or runner changes — generated problems are constrained to what the existing sandbox/judge already executes (fn and class modes).
No key-encryption or key-migration machinery beyond enter/update/delete of a key in localStorage.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is about machinery — LLM provider adapters, browser-direct API calls, localStorage persistence, runtime bank merging, and a versioned JSON backup format — with no business entities, rules, or workflows a domain expert would recognize; the review-before-add gate is a UI workflow, not a business process.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The runtime-merged set of built-in PROBLEM_BANK problems plus accepted generated problems; the set a user browses and solves.
An LLM-produced payload parsed into the Problem shape (slug, num, title, difficulty, tags, fnName, mode, starter, tests, hints, desc), pending or accepted.
The accept/discard gate a generated problem passes through, showing title, signature, and test preview before it can enter the problem bank.
Enforcement at accept time that a generated problem does not collide (by slug, title, or signature) with PROBLEM_BANK or already-accepted generated problems.
The abstraction over Anthropic Messages API, OpenAI Chat Completions, and OpenAI-compatible local /v1/chat/completions endpoints that returns a parsed generated problem.
The versioned single-JSON backup and restore of the persisted Zustand slice (lang, split, lastSlug, problems with solvedAt/js/ts/cases/subs) plus the generated problem bank.
Browser storage holding app state under the leetlab.v2 key and API keys under a separate key; the mechanism that makes generated problems survive reloads.
The gate that parses raw LLM text into the exact Problem shape and rejects or re-prompts malformed output before a generated problem can be accepted.
The final cross-cutting check that the whole feature passes npm run build (tsc + vite) and npm run lint.

discoveryFindings.finding: The bank is a static `export const PROBLEM_BANK: Problem[]` with 30 entries. `store.getProblem` does `PROBLEM_BANK.find(p => p.slug === slug)` (no generated fallback). Sidebar.tsx and Topbar.tsx import PROBLEM_BANK directly and iterate it / use `.length` for counts and progress segments. DescPane, EditorPane, CodeEditor, Drawer all reach problems through `store.getProblem`/`getProblemState`/`getCases`, not the bank directly.
discoveryFindings.implication: A runtime-merged bank (built-ins + generated) only needs a merge point in `getProblem` plus a merged list/count source for Sidebar and Topbar. DescPane/EditorPane/CodeEditor/Drawer automatically work once `getProblem` merges.

discoveryFindings.finding: Topbar derives progress segments and the solved-count denominator from `PROBLEM_BANK.length` (not a hardcoded 6). AGENTS.md claims it hardcodes 6, but the actual code at Topbar.tsx:24 uses `Array.from({ length: PROBLEM_BANK.length })`.
discoveryFindings.implication: Do not trust the stale AGENTS.md claim; Topbar already reacts to bank length, but it still reads the static bank rather than a merged set.

discoveryFindings.finding: Zustand persist key is `leetlab.v2`; `partialize` persists exactly `{ lang, split, lastSlug, problems }`. `problems` is a `Record<slug, { subs, cases, js, ts, solvedAt }>`; `cases: null` means 'fall back to builtin tests'. Persist config has no `version`, no `migrate`, no `storage` override (defaults to localStorage). Intentionally ephemeral fields NOT persisted: caseMarks, lastRuns, tsStatus, activeResultTab, currentSlug, selectedCaseIdx, filter, status, search, cursorLine, cursorCol.
discoveryFindings.implication: Full-state export/import must be defined against exactly `{lang, split, lastSlug, problems}` plus the new generated-problem slice. `currentSlug` is not persisted and is never restored from `lastSlug`.

discoveryFindings.finding: `getProblemState` lazily writes a default ProblemState into `problems` on first access (mutates during render). `subs` is capped at the last 60. There is no version bump in the persist config today.
discoveryFindings.implication: Adding a new persisted slice (e.g. `generatedProblems`) to `partialize` merges over the initial default on rehydrate, so an additive field with a safe default likely survives without a key bump — but AGENTS.md documents 'changing persisted fields requires a key bump or migration'. The plan should explicitly decide bump (`leetlab.v3`) vs additive default.

discoveryFindings.finding: Problem shape is exactly `{ slug, num, title, difficulty: 'Easy'|'Medium'|'Hard', tags, fnName, mode: 'fn'|'class', starter: {js, ts}, tests: ProblemTest[], hints, desc }`. `ProblemTest` is `{ in?: unknown[], calls?: unknown[][], out: unknown }`. The sandbox (sandbox.worker.ts) calls fn mode with `...c.input`, awaits thenables, and compares with a custom NaN-aware structural `deepEq`; class mode treats `tests[].calls` as `[['Ctor', args], ['method', args], ...]`, normalizes `undefined` returns to `null`.
discoveryFindings.implication: Generated problems must be parsed into exactly this shape. Validation of 'does this judge correctly' can and should reuse the existing worker via `useRunCode.run(code, problem, parseCases(...))`.

discoveryFindings.finding: The bank uses sparse real LeetCode numbers (1, 3, 9, 20, 21, 42, 56, 70, 104, 136, 155, 200, 206, 226, 232, 242, 322, 704) plus a custom 8000-series (8001-8012). `slug` is the real lookup key; `num` is cosmetic but rendered in the UI as `#num`.
discoveryFindings.implication: Generated problems need a non-colliding numbering scheme (continue the 8000+ series or add a new range) and unique slugs.

discoveryFindings.finding: `getDefaultCases` caches builtin TestCase arrays in a module-level `Map<string, TestCase[]>` keyed by `problem.slug`, and `getCases()` returns `ps?.cases || getDefaultCases(prob)`.
discoveryFindings.implication: A generated problem with a slug colliding with a built-in (or a previously generated one) would share/poison this cache and collide in `problems`. Dedupe by slug is not just cosmetic — it protects the case cache and per-slug state.

discoveryFindings.finding: TypeScript is loaded at runtime from the jsDelivr CDN (`typescript@5.4.5`, tsCompiler.ts) with a regex `stripTypes` fallback; tsCheck.ts lazily fetches `lib.d.ts` files from jsDelivr and caches them in memory. The worker protocol is: post `{code, name, mode, cases}`, receive `compile` | `case {i, ms, ok, hasExp, pass, output, error, logs}` | `console` | `done`, with a 6s timeout in useRunCode.
discoveryFindings.implication: The 'does this generated problem judge correctly' acceptance gate can be validated by running the generated starter/tests through `useRunCode` in-browser before persisting — no new execution engine needed.

discoveryFindings.finding: There is no OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama code, no `fetch` to external APIs (the only `fetch` in src is tsCheck.ts pulling TS lib.d.ts from jsDelivr), and no `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` usage outside zustand's persist middleware. There is no settings/preferences UI and no import/export code.
discoveryFindings.implication: Provider adapters (Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible local), the API-key storage key (e.g. `leetlab.apiKeys`), and the versioned JSON export/import format are all net-new; nothing to reconcile against.

discoveryFindings.area: UI patterns & entry point for Generate/Import/Export
discoveryFindings.finding: Topbar has no action buttons at all (brand, progress segments, solved count, TS badge). There is no modal/overlay/dialog component in the codebase; the only 'Drawer' is the bottom testcase/result/console panel. The only existing form inputs are the sidebar search box and the case input/expected textareas. DescPane's tab buttons (`#tabDesc`/`#tabSubs`) have no `onClick` handlers, so the Submissions tab is unreachable by click (known regression).
discoveryFindings.implication: The Generate/Import/Export entry points will be new Topbar (or new component) buttons, and the review-before-add flow plus API-key form is net-new modal/drawer UI.

discoveryFindings.finding: Single zustand store `useAppStore` created with `persist`. Actions use `set`/`get`; several helpers (`getProblem`, `getProblemState`, `getCases`) are store actions. Import style is mixed: `App.tsx`/`hooks/`/`infrastructure/` use `@` aliases; components use relative imports.
discoveryFindings.implication: New store fields/actions (generatedProblems slice, accept/discard, key storage or a separate key module, import/restore actions) should follow the existing interface + implementation pattern in store.ts.

discoveryFindings.finding: The `docs/done/src-vs-prototype-refactor-roadmap.md` is partly stale against current src: the run-submit-same-handler finding is fixed, the TLE-drops-run-results finding is fixed, and Topbar already uses `PROBLEM_BANK.length`. Still live: DescPane tab buttons have no onClick (submissions tab unreachable).
discoveryFindings.implication: The plan should not treat the roadmap's stale findings as pending work. The main live regression that affects new UI placement is DescPane's unwired tabs.

discoveryFindings.finding: Store initial state sets `lastSlug` and `currentSlug` to `PROBLEM_BANK[0].slug` ('two-sum'), and Topbar/Sidebar count denominators assume a non-empty PROBLEM_BANK.
discoveryFindings.implication: Import validation must reject/repair a file whose `lastSlug` or `currentSlug` does not resolve in the merged bank.

requiredMaterials.name: Anthropic API key (development/test)

phases.name: API key storage (leetlab.apiKeys localStorage persistence)
phases.goal: Create the localStorage-backed module holding user-entered provider API keys under the dedicated leetlab.apiKeys key, with masked reads and a single import point so keys stay out of full-state export.
inputs: Discovery: no existing settings or localStorage code outside zustand persist middleware
Assumption: keys stored under leetlab.apiKeys, masked in the UI, excluded from export/import
Required material: developer-held Anthropic/OpenAI test keys used only at runtime, never embedded in source
phases.expectedResult: A single module src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts (getKey/setKey/clearKey under the leetlab.apiKeys key plus a redact helper) that provider adapters and the settings UI consume and that full-state export explicitly omits.
phases.compensation: Delete the module and clear the leetlab.apiKeys localStorage entry; no other subsystem holds key state because adapters and UI read keys only through this module.

rubric.label: All key state scoped to leetlab.apiKeys
rubric.ruleStatement: Every provider API key read and write is scoped to the single `leetlab.apiKeys` localStorage key; no key material ever lands in the `leetlab.v2` persisted slice or any other storage key.
passCriteria: The module defines exactly one storage-key constant whose value is `leetlab.apiKeys`, and getKey/setKey/clearKey operate only on that constant.
A repo-wide grep for the string `leetlab.apiKeys` shows it referenced only inside src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts and at consumer call sites — never in the Zustand persist config or state slice.
A grep for API-key-shaped writes (setItem of `leetlab.v2` or any key other than `leetlab.apiKeys`) finds none in the module or its consumers.
Serializing the persisted slice (`localStorage.getItem('leetlab.v2')`) after setKey shows no provider key field.
failureExamples: setKey writes the key into the existing `leetlab.v2` JSON blob instead of a dedicated key.
The module hard-codes a different storage key (e.g. `leetlab.keys`) while the docs and consumers expect `leetlab.apiKeys`.
The persisted Zustand state contains an `apiKeys` field.

rubric.label: Keys are redacted for display and never logged
rubric.ruleStatement: A `redact` helper returns a masked form of a key suitable for UI readback, and no code path logs or surfaces full key material outside the runtime provider call.
passCriteria: `redact(key)` exists and returns a string with the body masked (at most a few trailing characters visible) for typical key shapes such as `sk-ant-...` and `sk-...`.
`redact` handles short and empty inputs without error and never returns the full input for a non-empty value.
No `console.log`/debug statement in the module or settings UI prints a key value.
Any readback in the settings UI is rendered from `redact` output, not from raw getKey.
failureExamples: `redact` returns the input unchanged.
A debug `console.log(key)` in setKey or getKey prints the full secret.
The settings UI displays the raw stored key back to the user.

rubric.label: Key material excluded from export/import path
rubric.ruleStatement: The module is a standalone infra module that is not wired into Zustand persist or the full-state export/import path, so key material can never appear in exported backup JSON or be restored by an import.
passCriteria: src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts imports no Zustand store and does not reference `persist`, `partialize`, or the `leetlab.v2` slice.
The persisted-slice definition (persist config) contains no apiKeys field and the full-state export function has no import of the apiKeys module.
A grep for `getItem('leetlab.apiKeys')` outside the module and its explicit consumers finds none.
A dry-run serialization of the store state after setKey contains no provider key values.
failureExamples: A full-state export JSON contains `"anthropicApiKey": "sk-..."`.
The Zustand persist `partialize` includes an apiKeys field, sweeping keys into every backup.
The import routine writes restored key values back into the apiKeys module.

rubric.label: Adapters and UI read keys only through the module
rubric.ruleStatement: Provider adapters and the settings UI obtain key values exclusively through this module's getKey/setKey API; no other file touches localStorage for API key material.
passCriteria: A repo-wide grep for `localStorage` shows no getItem/setItem calls for key material outside src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts.
Provider adapters import `getKey` from the module and never call `localStorage` themselves.
The settings UI persists keys only via `setKey` and displays only via `redact`.
failureExamples: The Anthropic provider adapter reads `localStorage.getItem('anthropicKey')` directly.
A settings component writes `localStorage.setItem('leetlab.apiKeys', ...)` bypassing the module.
Two files store keys under different key names or shapes.

rubric.label: Per-provider round-trip, reload safety, and full clear
rubric.ruleStatement: The module stores keys per provider (anthropic/openai/local) under the single `leetlab.apiKeys` key; setKey/getKey/clearKey round-trip correctly and survive reloads, clearKey fully removes the entry, and no real key material is committed to source.
passCriteria: setKey('anthropic', a) then setKey('openai', o) both round-trip through getKey without clobbering each other.
setKey(p,k) → getKey(p) === k, and clearKey(p) → getKey(p) is null.
A full clearKey leaves `localStorage.getItem('leetlab.apiKeys')` null (entry removed), and a fresh page load shows no key.
Values set then read after a simulated reload are identical; malformed stored JSON returns null rather than throwing.
A grep of committed source for provider-key patterns finds no real secret values.
failureExamples: Storing an OpenAI key overwrites the Anthropic key because the module has a single key slot.
clearKey sets the entry to `''` or `{}` instead of removing it.
getKey throws on corrupt JSON, crashing the settings UI.
A real test key string is committed into source.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is key material leaking into the `leetlab.v2` persisted slice or a consumer writing localStorage directly — centralize every key read/write in `src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts`, strip any `apiKeys` field from the Zustand persist `partialize`, and re-grep the repo to confirm no other file touches key storage.

phases.name: Provider adapters (Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible local)
phases.goal: Implement browser-direct provider adapters that POST the generation prompt to the Anthropic Messages API, OpenAI Chat Completions, or a user-configured OpenAI-compatible local /v1/chat/completions endpoint and return raw model text, with the mandatory Anthropic browser-access header, correct auth, current model constants, and CORS/network error classification.
inputs: api-key-storage phase
Required material: Anthropic Messages API contract incl. anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access header and a current model ID
Required material: OpenAI Chat Completions contract incl. choices[0].message.content extraction and a default model
Required material: running OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (Ollama/LM Studio) for validation
Risk: browser CORS on Anthropic/OpenAI/local endpoints yields opaque network failures that must be classified
phases.expectedResult: Provider adapters generateProblemText({provider, apiKey, baseUrl?, model, prompt}) -> raw text for anthropic/openai/local, a shared classified error result (auth vs 4xx vs CORS/network vs 5xx), and a provider+model picker constant list. No Problem parsing yet.

rubric.label: Classified error result across all providers
rubric.ruleStatement: Every adapter failure resolves to the shared classified error result that distinguishes auth errors, other 4xx client errors, CORS/network failures, and 5xx server errors; no raw or unclassified error escapes the adapter surface.
passCriteria: Unit tests assert 401/403 from any provider map to the auth error category
Unit tests assert a TypeError / 'Failed to fetch' (CORS block or offline) maps to the cors-network category, distinct from auth
Unit tests assert 5xx maps to the server error category, distinct from 4xx
The returned error result carries a stable machine-readable category field
No call site has to string-match fetch error messages to know the category
failureExamples: A CORS failure and an invalid-key failure both surface as the same generic 'Failed to fetch'
The adapter throws a raw Error whose message callers must parse to classify
5xx and 4xx are lumped into one generic 'request failed' bucket

rubric.label: Correct per-provider auth and mandatory headers
rubric.ruleStatement: Each adapter sends the exact auth and required headers for its provider, including the mandatory Anthropic browser-direct header; the API key travels only in headers, never in the URL, request body, logs, or error output.
passCriteria: Anthropic requests include x-api-key, anthropic-version, content-type, and anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true
OpenAI and local requests include Authorization: Bearer <key> and content-type: application/json
No fetch call places the API key in the URL or query string
Header assertions exist in tests for each provider's outgoing request
The key value never appears in error messages, console output, or the provider/model constants
failureExamples: Anthropic call omits anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access and fails with 403 in the browser
The API key is interpolated into the request URL
Missing anthropic-version header yields a 400 from Anthropic
The key value shows up in a logged error or the picker constants

rubric.label: Correct response-shape extraction per provider
rubric.ruleStatement: Each adapter extracts and returns the raw model text using the correct response shape for its provider — choices[0].message.content for OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, content[0].text for Anthropic Messages — and returns a plain string, with no Problem-shape parsing.
passCriteria: OpenAI and local adapters read choices[0].message.content and return the trimmed text string
Anthropic adapter reads content[0].text and returns the trimmed text string
Non-2xx responses are routed to the classifier rather than treated as model text
Missing/empty content is surfaced as an explicit error, never returned as 'undefined'
The return value is raw text only; no Problem parsing or transformation happens in this phase
failureExamples: OpenAI adapter reads choices[0].text (the legacy chat shape) and returns undefined
Anthropic adapter returns the whole content array instead of the inner text
The adapter JSON.parses the model output into a Problem shape, pulling next-phase scope into this one

rubric.label: Single entry point, endpoint routing, and current model constants
rubric.ruleStatement: A single generateProblemText({provider, apiKey, baseUrl?, model, prompt}) entry point dispatches to the right provider adapter, honors a configurable baseUrl for local OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and returns raw text; the provider/model picker exposes current (non-deprecated) model IDs.
passCriteria: generateProblemText exists with the specified signature and returns a raw text string for provider 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'local'
The local provider POSTs to the configured baseUrl + '/v1/chat/completions'; the baseUrl override is honored
Anthropic and OpenAI use their correct default endpoints when baseUrl is omitted
The picker constant list contains current, non-deprecated model IDs
Provider wire format knowledge lives only in the adapter layer; callers receive a uniform raw-text result
failureExamples: generateProblemText is missing or has a different signature
The local endpoint hardcodes localhost:11434 instead of honoring baseUrl
The model list contains a deprecated/removed model ID
The local adapter always posts to the official OpenAI URL

rubric.label: Deterministic, side-effect-light adapters
rubric.ruleStatement: Adapters are deterministic with respect to their inputs: identical calls produce identical request shapes, no module-level mutable state alters behavior between calls, and the API key is passed per call rather than captured in module state.
passCriteria: Calling generateProblemText twice with identical args yields identical request shape (URL, headers, body)
No module-level mutable state (counters, caches, last-response) changes behavior between calls
The API key is a function parameter, not read from an imported module constant or global
Grep of the adapter module shows the key only flowing into request headers, never persisted or mutated
failureExamples: The adapter caches the last response and returns it for a different prompt
The API key is stashed in a module-level variable instead of passed per call
Repeated calls push onto a module-level array that changes the request body on the second call

phases.healerHint: The rubric most likely fails on error classification (CORS and auth both surfacing as one opaque 'Failed to fetch'), so extract a classifyError helper that maps TypeError to the cors-network category distinct from 401/403 and pin it with a mocked-fetch unit test — and if Anthropic 403s, double-check anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access is actually set on the request.

phases.name: Generated-problem persisted store slice with accept/discard and dedupe
phases.goal: Add a persisted generatedProblems slice to the Zustand store, settle the persist-key/version strategy for the new field, and implement acceptGeneratedProblem (dedupe by slug/title/signature against the problem bank plus non-colliding num assignment) and discardGeneratedProblem.
inputs: Discovery: leetlab.v2 partialize persists exactly {lang, split, lastSlug, problems}; no version/migrate configured today
Discovery: getDefaultCases module cache keyed by slug — slug dedupe protects the case cache and per-slug state
Discovery: numbering is sparse real LeetCode nums plus an 8000-series custom range; generated problems need a non-colliding scheme
Problem shape from src/domain/Problem.ts (slug, num, title, difficulty, tags, fnName, mode, starter, tests, hints, desc)
phases.expectedResult: Store exposes persisted generatedProblems (accepted generated problems survive reloads), acceptGeneratedProblem returning {ok:true} or {ok:false, reason: duplicate-slug|duplicate-title|duplicate-signature, collidingWith}, discardGeneratedProblem, and a documented additive-default-vs-leetlab.v3-bump decision with non-colliding num assignment.

rubric.label: Accepted generated problems persist across reloads
rubric.ruleStatement: Accepting a generated problem must write it into the persisted Zustand slice so that a full page reload rehydrates it from localStorage as part of the merged problem bank.
passCriteria: Accept a generated problem, then fully reload the app; the accepted problem is still present in the store and browsable in the merged bank.
The serialized state under the chosen persist key (leetlab.v2 or v3) contains the accepted generated problem.
The persist config (partialize/version) explicitly includes generatedProblems, and removing it from partialize demonstrably stops persistence.
failureExamples: Accepted problems vanish after reload even though they returned {ok:true} at accept time.
State is persisted under a new key with no migrate, so existing users lose prior progress on the first load after upgrade.

rubric.label: Dedupe against the merged problem bank
rubric.ruleStatement: acceptGeneratedProblem must reject any generated problem whose slug, title, or signature collides with a built-in PROBLEM_BANK entry or an already-accepted generated problem, returning {ok:false, reason, collidingWith} so the review gate can explain the rejection.
passCriteria: A generated problem whose slug equals a built-in PROBLEM_BANK entry returns {ok:false, reason:'duplicate-slug', collidingWith:<that entry>}.

Double-accepting the same payload is a no-op duplicate, never a second insertion.
A non-colliding generated problem returns {ok:true} and is stored exactly once.
failureExamples: A duplicate slug is silently accepted and shadows the built-in entry when the bank is merged at read time.
Only slug is checked; title or signature collisions slip through.
Returned reason or collidingWith is wrong or absent.

rubric.label: Non-colliding num assignment
rubric.ruleStatement: Each accepted generated problem receives a num that does not collide with real LeetCode nums, the 8000-series custom range, or any other accepted generated problem, and the assignment is stable given the same accepted set.
passCriteria: Two accepted generated problems always receive distinct nums.
Generated nums never equal any num present in PROBLEM_BANK.
The assignment is deterministic: discarding a generated problem and re-accepting the same payload reuses the freed slot rather than drifting.
failureExamples: Two generated problems share a num, breaking num-keyed routing/selection.
A generated num collides with a built-in num, making problem selection ambiguous.

rubric.label: Built-in problem bank is never mutated
rubric.ruleStatement: Accepting or discarding generated problems must never mutate, shadow, or reorder the built-in PROBLEM_BANK; generated problems live in their own slice and merge only at read time.
passCriteria: PROBLEM_BANK is unchanged (reference identity and length) after accept and discard operations.
The merged bank is derived from PROBLEM_BANK + generatedProblems without writing back into PROBLEM_BANK.
Built-in per-slug state and the getDefaultCases cache keyed by slug are not clobbered by any generated problem.
failureExamples: Accepting a generated problem appends to or overwrites an entry in the built-in PROBLEM_BANK.
A generated problem with a colliding slug corrupts the built-in getDefaultCases cache.

rubric.label: Additive-default vs version-bump is decided and rollback-safe
rubric.ruleStatement: The persist strategy must either keep the additive field on leetlab.v2 (additive default) or, if bumped to leetlab.v3, ship a migrate that preserves prior state; the documented decision and the compensation path must leave built-in data and existing user state intact.
passCriteria: The additive-default-vs-v3-bump decision is documented in the store/persist config with rationale.
If a version bump was chosen, a migrate preserves {lang, split, lastSlug, problems} and any prior accepted generated problems — no silent data loss on first load after upgrade.
Reverting the change rehydrates defaults without throwing, and previously accepted generated problems are simply no longer read.
failureExamples: leetlab.v3 bump shipped without a migrate, so every existing user starts empty on upgrade.
Reverting the phase leaves a partially-written key or throws on load.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is the reload check — generatedProblems gets accepted into memory but is left out of the persist partialize (or dedupe is checked only against the generated list and not PROBLEM_BANK), so the fastest fix is to add generatedProblems to the partialize and include PROBLEM_BANK in the dedupe source, then re-run the accept-then-reload test.

rubric.label: Complete Problem shape or errors, never partial
rubric.ruleStatement: validateGeneratedProblem must return either a fully-populated Problem (every required field present and correctly typed) or an errors array — never a partial object with undefined fields, and never a throw on recoverable input. It must be deterministic.
passCriteria: Feeding rawText that omits or mistypes a required field returns {errors} listing the offending field, not a partial problem
Every field in an accepted problem is defined and has the declared type

rubric.label: Tests match the fnName + mode signature
rubric.ruleStatement: Every test must be runnable against the declared signature: in classic mode each test.in is an argument array matching fnName's parameters, and in class mode calls is a sequence of Ctor/method call sequences matching the class's method signatures.

rubric.label: Tests are JSON-serializable and round-trip losslessly

A unit test asserts accepted problems survive a full serialize→persist→rehydrate cycle unchanged

rubric.label: desc uses only the DescPane-renderable HTML vocabulary
rubric.ruleStatement: A generated desc must render correctly through DescPane, which renders via dangerouslySetInnerHTML with a specific vocabulary. rubric.label: hints is a strict string array
rubric.ruleStatement: The hints field must be an array of strings (empty array allowed) matching the Problem shape's declared type.
passCriteria: An accepted problem always has hints typed as string[]

rubric.label: Re-prompt is bounded, corrective, and malformed output never persists
rubric.ruleStatement: On validation failure, the loop must re-prompt the provider adapter a bounded number of times (max attempts), each retry carrying corrective feedback derived from the prior errors, and must terminate in a rejectable error so a malformed generated problem can never reach accept or localStorage.
passCriteria: With a provider stub that always returns malformed output, the loop terminates after exactly max attempts (no infinite loop) and surfaces a rejectable error type

A rejected malformed problem is still persisted to localStorage
The re-prompt loop bypasses validateGeneratedProblem and accepts the first raw parse

Discovery: store.getProblem does PROBLEM_BANK.find only (no generated fallback)
Discovery: Sidebar imports PROBLEM_BANK directly for counts/status/filter; Topbar uses PROBLEM_BANK.length for segments and the solved denominator

rubric.label: getProblem resolves accepted generated problems

rubric.label: Sidebar derives list, counts, and status from the merged bank

passCriteria: Grep over Sidebar shows no direct PROBLEM_BANK.length / filter / find for counts or status; data comes from a store-derived merged source
With a seeded accepted generated problem, the sidebar lists it alongside built-ins with correct difficulty, tags, and unsolved status

rubric.label: Topbar segments and solved denominator count the merged bank

passCriteria: With K built-in and M accepted generated problems, the solved denominator is K+M, not PROBLEM_BANK.length

rubric.label: PROBLEM_BANK is never mutated by the merge

passCriteria: PROBLEM_BANK.length is identical before and after accepting generated problems and reloads

rubric.label: Merged bank is idempotent and stable across reads and reloads
rubric.ruleStatement: The merged list/count is a pure, deterministic function of (PROBLEM_BANK plus accepted generatedProblems): repeated reads return the same length and order, with no duplicates or drift across reloads.
passCriteria: Calling the merged-list selector twice returns equal lengths and identical ordering

rubric.label: Built-in-only path is unchanged when no generated problems exist
rubric.ruleStatement: When the generated bank is empty, merged behavior is identical to the pre-phase behavior: sidebar counts, topbar denominator, and problem resolution match pure PROBLEM_BANK exactly.
passCriteria: With an empty generatedProblems slice, the merged list equals PROBLEM_BANK in length, order, and content

phases.name: Review-before-add gate (accept/discard with visible dedupe)

rubric.label: Review screen renders the actual pending problem
rubric.ruleStatement: The review screen displays title, signature (fnName + mode), and test preview sourced from the pendingGenerated in-memory state — not placeholders, stale content from a prior generation, or a re-triggered fetch/generate.

rubric.ruleStatement: Accepting a generated problem that passes dedupe calls acceptGeneratedProblem, makes the accepted problem appear in the merged problem bank, surfaces the acceptance visibly, clears the review queue, and never double-adds under repeated clicks.

rubric.ruleStatement: Discarding a pending generated problem calls discardGeneratedProblem, removes it from the review queue, and leaves the problem bank exactly as it was — nothing added, nothing modified — while being a harmless no-op when the queue is already empty.

A base URL or model field accidentally captures a key because the keys store is merged wholesale

rubric.label: Versioned, single, canonical document
rubric.ruleStatement: The export is one versioned JSON file shaped exactly `{version, persisted, generatedProblems}` — the canonical spec the import validates against.
passCriteria: The document has a top-level `version` field whose value is a defined schema version and changes when the schema changes
Export produces exactly one `.json` file via one download (Blob)
The top-level keys are exactly `version`, `persisted`, and `generatedProblems`
failureExamples: No `version` field, or `version` is a hardcoded string with no defined meaning
Export downloads two files or prints JSON to the console without a file download
Top-level shape has extra keys the import validator does not expect

rubric.label: Valid, re-parseable, lossless JSON
rubric.ruleStatement: The downloaded file is valid JSON that parses back into the exact state without loss or drift, so it is usable as the source for the import/restore.
passCriteria: The downloaded file parses with `JSON.parse` without error
Re-parsing and diffing against live state: `lang`, `split`, `lastSlug` match exactly and problem content round-trips without drift
Numeric values such as `num` and `solvedAt` retain their types and `undefined` fields are omitted consistently
failureExamples: The file fails to parse (truncated download, double-stringified JSON, or `NaN`/`Infinity` values)
`solvedAt` or `num` become strings, or a field disappears
The file is valid JSON but contains only a summary instead of the full state

rubric.label: Repeatable export with no state mutation
rubric.ruleStatement: Exporting is a pure read: re-exporting identical state yields data-identical documents, and the action never mutates app state.
passCriteria: Two exports from identical state contain identical problem data and ordering
The export action writes nothing to `leetlab.v2` or the generated bank
failureExamples: Each export inserts or reorders entries, so two backups differ for no state reason
Invoking export mutates persisted state
Serialization itself triggers a persistence write that changes the data being backed up

phases.healerHint: If the gate fails, the export payload was almost certainly built by spreading a whole store or by omitting a field — construct the JSON from an explicit allowlist ({version, persisted:{lang, split, lastSlug, problems}, generatedProblems}) and grep the downloaded file for `apiKey`/`sk-` before re-testing.

phases.name: Validated full-state JSON import
phases.goal: Import the versioned JSON: validate version and schema, restore the persisted slice and generated problem bank atomically, fail with a clear error on malformed or wrong-version files without touching the live store, and reject files whose lastSlug/currentSlug do not resolve in the merged bank or whose generated problems collide with PROBLEM_BANK.
inputs: full-state-export phase (format and version constant)
runtime-merged-bank phase (merged lookup to validate lastSlug/currentSlug)
Discovery: getProblemState lazily writes defaults during render; initial state assumes a non-empty PROBLEM_BANK
phases.expectedResult: A Topbar 'Import' action + file picker that validates version/schema, atomically restores the persisted slice and generatedProblems (or leaves the live store untouched with a visible error on any failure), and verifies slug uniqueness and lastSlug/currentSlug resolution.
phases.compensation: Import writes the persisted slice and generatedProblems into localStorage; rollback means re-importing a prior export. The import action must keep a pre-import snapshot of the persisted slice and generatedProblems to restore on any validation failure, and a later rollback of this phase only affects users who voluntarily imported.

rubric.label: Version gate rejects wrong-version files
rubric.ruleStatement: Import compares the file's version against the current export version constant before any store mutation; files with a missing, malformed, or unsupported version are rejected with a visible error and the live store and localStorage remain unchanged.
passCriteria: Importing JSON whose version differs from the current export version constant surfaces a clear visible error and aborts before writing
Importing JSON with a missing or non-string version field surfaces a clear visible error and aborts
After each rejected import, the persisted Zustand slice and generatedProblems in localStorage are byte-for-byte identical to the pre-import snapshot
failureExamples: A file with the wrong version is applied and overwrites live state
Version mismatch throws an unhandled exception instead of a user-facing error
A downgrade or future-version file is accepted because the version constant is never compared

rubric.label: Malformed or schema-invalid files fail cleanly
rubric.ruleStatement: The importer validates the parsed JSON against the full-state schema (shape and types) and reports the failing field; malformed input never crashes the app and never mutates the live store.
passCriteria: Feeding a truncated/empty file or non-JSON text shows a visible error and leaves state untouched
Feeding valid JSON whose root is not an object, or that misses required keys, shows a visible error that names the missing field
Type mismatches are caught with a visible error rather than a runtime crash or silent defaulting
failureExamples: Pasting a malformed file crashes the app or resets state to defaults
Missing required keys are silently defaulted, producing a partial restore that looks successful
A schema error leaves localStorage partially rewritten before aborting

rubric.label: Failed imports roll back to the pre-import snapshot
rubric.ruleStatement: Every import path takes a pre-import snapshot of the persisted slice and generatedProblems; any validation failure restores that snapshot so the live store and localStorage are never partially or corruptly written.
passCriteria: The code captures a snapshot of the persisted slice and generatedProblems before applying any import
Each distinct failure path (version, schema, slug resolution, dedupe) leaves the in-memory store and the leetlab.v2 localStorage key identical to the snapshot
A fault injected mid-apply restores the snapshot instead of leaving a half-applied state
failureExamples: A failure mid-apply leaves the store with imported problems but the old progress, or vice versa
The snapshot is captured after some writes have already occurred, so rollback is partial
localStorage retains a corrupted or partially written value after a failed import

rubric.label: lastSlug/currentSlug must resolve in the merged bank
rubric.ruleStatement: Import rejects files whose lastSlug or currentSlug does not resolve to a problem in the runtime-merged bank (built-in PROBLEM_BANK plus the imported generatedProblems), because a dangling slug would break the solve screen and reviewer UI.
passCriteria: Importing a file whose lastSlug/currentSlug points at a problem present only in the imported generatedProblems succeeds and the slug resolves after merge
Importing a file whose lastSlug/currentSlug matches no problem in the merged bank shows a visible error naming the slug
The resolution check consults the merged bank, not PROBLEM_BANK or generatedProblems alone
failureExamples: A file with a nonexistent lastSlug imports successfully, leaving the app pointing at a missing problem
Slug resolution is checked against PROBLEM_BANK only, so a valid generated-problem slug is wrongly rejected
A dangling currentSlug slips through and the solve screen renders blank after import

rubric.label: Imported generated problems dedupe against PROBLEM_BANK
rubric.ruleStatement: Import rejects files whose generatedProblems collide with PROBLEM_BANK by slug, title, or signature; no duplicate problem may enter the merged bank through the import path.
passCriteria: Importing generatedProblems whose slug, title, or signature duplicates a PROBLEM_BANK entry is rejected with a visible error naming the collision
Colliding files leave the live store and the merged bank unchanged
Generated problems that are internally unique and non-colliding import successfully
failureExamples: A generated problem duplicating a built-in slug enters the bank, producing duplicate entries
Title-case or signature collisions are ignored
Import silently overwrites a built-in problem instead of rejecting the collision

rubric.label: Successful import restores full state and persists
rubric.ruleStatement: A valid export, when imported, reproduces the exact persisted slice (lang, split, lastSlug, problems with solvedAt/js/ts/cases/subs) and generatedProblems in the live store and in localStorage, so a reload keeps the restored state.
passCriteria: Export full state, mutate several fields, then import the export; the live app reflects the restored values
All sub-fields of problems (solvedAt, js, ts, cases, subs) are present and correct after import
After import, a page reload re-reads the imported state from localStorage with no loss
failureExamples: Import restores progress but drops saved code or custom test cases
Imported generatedProblems appear in the merged bank but are not written to localStorage
Import works in memory but never persists, so the restored state is lost on refresh

phases.healerHint: The most likely miss is a validation path that isn't actually wired to reject (version never compared, or slug/dedupe checked against PROBLEM_BANK only), so write four fixture-driven import tests — malformed, wrong-version, dangling slug, and a PROBLEM_BANK collision — that each assert the pre-import snapshot is restored byte-for-byte.

phases.name: Build and lint verification
phases.goal: Verify the complete feature passes the project's static checks — npm run build (tsc + vite) and npm run lint — with all new modules, store wiring, and UI in place.
inputs: All prior phases
phases.expectedResult: npm run build and npm run lint both pass with the provider adapters, generated-problem slice, merged bank read path, review UI, and export/import landed.

rubric.label: No suppressed type errors
rubric.ruleStatement: The build (tsc) passes without suppression crutches: no `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, or unsafe `as any`/`as unknown as Problem` escapes mask a real type defect in the new provider adapters, generated-problem slice, or merged bank read path.
passCriteria: The tsc step of `npm run build` exits 0 with no `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-expect-error` comments in any new module
Provider adapter LLM responses are validated into the Problem shape with type guards or field-level parsing, not blanket `as Problem` casts
A grep for `as any|as unknown|@ts-ignore|@ts-expect-error` across the feature's source returns zero matches
failureExamples: A `@ts-ignore` sits above a mismatch between the provider's raw response fields and the required Problem shape
The merged bank read path casts persisted generated-problem JSON with `as Problem`
tsc is green only because every parse site ends in `as unknown as Problem`

rubric.label: Deterministic, repeatable build
rubric.ruleStatement: The build is repeatable and idempotent: consecutive `npm run build` runs from a clean tree both exit 0 and produce identical output, with no cache- or order-dependent failures.
passCriteria: `npm run build` run twice back-to-back exits 0 both times with no warnings
Deleting `dist/` and rebuilding regenerates output without errors
A fresh checkout (clean `dist`) builds successfully on the first attempt
failureExamples: The second build fails with a module-not-found that only appears after a clean
The build only succeeds after an unrelated `npm run dev` has warmed the cache
Generated `dist` files differ between identical runs

rubric.label: Zero lint violations in new modules
rubric.ruleStatement: `npm run lint` exits 0 with zero errors and zero warnings across every new module, including `no-unused-vars`/`no-unused-imports`, `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, and `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` in the review and generate-settings UI.
passCriteria: Lint reports 0 errors and 0 warnings for every file added or touched by the feature
No unused imports, unused local variables, or orphaned exported components remain
`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` passes for every effect in the review and generate-settings UI
failureExamples: A provider adapter imports a validation helper it never uses, flagged as an unused-import warning
The review UI's accept/discard effect has a missing dependency that lint flags
An orphaned `GenerateSettingsModal` component is exported but never imported

rubric.label: No API key material in source or bundle
rubric.ruleStatement: Because the feature handles user-entered provider API keys, the committed source and built bundle contain no real or placeholder key material, and API keys are excluded from the full-state export/import JSON so a backup file never carries credentials.
passCriteria: A scan of `src/`, `dist/`, and committed test fixtures for `sk-`, `sk-ant-`, `sk-proj-` returns zero matches
Provider-adapter code references no `.env`-injected secret (keys are read only from localStorage at runtime)
The full-state export schema omits the API-key localStorage key
failureExamples: A placeholder `sk-ant-...` key is committed in a provider adapter example or test fixture
The provider adapter imports `import.meta.env.VITE_ANTHROPIC_KEY`
The exported backup JSON includes the API-key storage key

rubric.label: Built-in problem bank never mutated
rubric.ruleStatement: The merged bank read path is side-effect free on the built-in PROBLEM_BANK: accepted generated problems live in their own localStorage slice and are merged read-only, so accepting, editing, or discarding a generated problem cannot mutate or corrupt the built-in set (rollback-safe).
passCriteria: `PROBLEM_BANK` is frozen or never written to; no `.push`, `.splice`, `.sort`, or `.pop` is called on the built-in array anywhere in the merged read path
Generated problems persist under the separate generated-bank localStorage key and the merge is a pure read-time concat/dedupe
Discarding all generated problems restores exactly the built-in set the user started with
failureExamples: `PROBLEM_BANK.push(generated)` mutates the built-in array at accept time
The dedupe step sorts the shared array in place
Removing a generated problem leaves the merged array corrupted because the underlying array was modified

phases.healerHint: The build/lint most likely fails on `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` or a `@ts-ignore` where a provider response is forced into the Problem shape — replace the `any`/`as unknown as Problem` with a field-level type-guard parser that validates the LLM payload, which clears tsc and lint at the same site.

successCriteria: Done when (1) a user can pick a provider (Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible local), enter an API key persisted to localStorage, and generate a valid Problem (both fn and class modes) that appears in a review screen showing title, signature (fnName + mode), and test preview; (2) Accept enforces dedupe against PROBLEM_BANK and already-accepted generated problems — slug/title/signature collisions are rejected with a visible message, never silently added — and the accepted problem is persisted so it appears in the problem list and in getProblem/sidebar alongside built-ins across reloads; (3) Discard leaves the bank unchanged; (4) Export writes a single versioned JSON capturing the persisted Zustand slice (lang, split, lastSlug, problems: solvedAt, js/ts, cases, subs) plus generated problems, and Import validates and restores it so the app behaves identically, while malformed or wrong-version files fail with a clear error and leave the live store untouched; (5) malformed LLM output is re-prompted or rejected, never persisted; (6) `npm run build` (tsc + vite) and `npm run lint` pass.

api-key-storage: A single module src/infrastructure/apiKeys.ts (getKey/setKey/clearKey under the leetlab.apiKeys key plus a redact helper) that provider adapters and the settings UI consume and that full-state export explicitly omits.

provider-adapters: Provider adapters generateProblemText({provider, apiKey, baseUrl?, model, prompt}) -> raw text for anthropic/openai/local, a shared classified error result (auth vs 4xx vs CORS/network vs 5xx), and a provider+model picker constant list. No Problem parsing yet.

generated-problem-slice: Store exposes persisted generatedProblems (accepted generated problems survive reloads), acceptGeneratedProblem returning {ok:true} or {ok:false, reason, collidingWith}, discardGeneratedProblem, and a documented additive-default-vs-leetlab.v3-bump decision with non-colliding num assignment.
output-validation-reprompt: validateGeneratedProblem(rawText) -> {problem} | {errors} plus a bounded re-prompt loop ending in a rejectable error, so malformed generated problems never reach accept.
runtime-merged-bank: getProblem resolves accepted generated problems and Sidebar/Topbar derive their lists/counts from the merged bank across reloads without mutating PROBLEM_BANK.

generate-settings-ui: A Topbar 'Generate' button opening a modal where the user picks a provider/model, enters and saves a masked API key, triggers generation, sees loading and classified errors, and on success has a validated generated problem held in an in-memory pending state ready for review.

review-before-add-ui: The accept/discard gate: Accept persists the generated problem when dedupe passes and shows a visible duplicate message when it fails (never silently adding); Discard leaves the bank unchanged and clears the review queue.
full-state-export: A Topbar 'Export' action serializing {version, persisted:{lang, split, lastSlug, problems}, generatedProblems} to one versioned JSON file and triggering a download.

full-state-import: A Topbar 'Import' action + file picker that validates version/schema, atomically restores the persisted slice and generatedProblems (or leaves the live store untouched with a visible error), and verifies slug uniqueness and lastSlug/currentSlug resolution.
build-lint-verify: npm run build and npm run lint both pass with the provider adapters, generated-problem slice, merged bank read path, review UI, and export/import landed.
deferred: No backend/proxy for LLM calls — browser-direct only, per the user's access model; there is no server to hold keys or relay requests.
No authentication, authorization, or multi-user sync — this is a single-browser local app with no user accounts.
No editing or management of generated problems after acceptance (no modifying tests/starter of an already-added generated problem).
No persistence or review history for discarded problems — the review queue is session-only, no recycle bin.
No cost/rate-limit management or streaming/abort UX for generation (no request budgets, token counters, or pricing display).
No new problem kinds or runner changes — generated problems are constrained to what the existing sandbox/judge already executes (fn and class modes).
No key-encryption or key-migration machinery beyond enter/update/delete of a key in localStorage.
Recycle bin / review history for discarded generated problems — fails YAGNI gate 1 (not asked for; assumption explicitly states discarded problems are not persisted).

Persisting intentionally ephemeral store fields (caseMarks, lastRuns, tsStatus, activeResultTab, selection) in full-state export — fails gates 1/2 (the requested field list is solvedAt/js/ts/cases/subs only; expanding the persist boundary is scope creep).
Provider plugin system / dynamic adapter registry — fails YAGNI gate 3 (only three concrete adapters exist today; a registry is speculative abstraction).
Token streaming of generation output — fails YAGNI gate 1 (not asked for; the review screen shows the final result).
Prompt/parameter customization UI (temperature, system-prompt editor) — fails gates 1/3 (not asked for; speculative).

Complex zustand migrate/version-bump migration — fails gates 2/3 (an additive generatedProblems field with a safe default rehydrates without a key bump; a migration is only warranted if the slice phase lands on leetlab.v3).
Exporting/importing API keys as part of full-state backup — fails YAGNI gate 1 (spec explicitly excludes keys to avoid spreading credentials).
